_comment: Single source of truth for every South African tax figure this site publishes. Before this file existed the brackets lived in TWO places — js/income-tax-calculator.js as data and content/guide-rates.html as a readable table — and nothing but a regex-scraping validator held them together. Every figure a calculator needs, and every figure the rate tables show, now comes from here. build.py renders the bracket tables from it and emits js/tax-rates.js for the browser. Add a new tax year as a new key under `years`, point `current` at it, and both the tables and the calculators follow.
_updating: After a Budget: add the new year, move `current`, then run `python build.py --check`. The check proves every cumulative `base` equals the tax at the top of the bracket below it, and that each threshold equals its rebate divided by the first bracket rate. A mistyped digit fails the build rather than silently shipping confident wrong answers.
_provisional_rules: The provisional tax rules below do not change from year to year and so are not stored per year. Estimates may not fall below the BASIC AMOUNT — the taxable income per the latest assessment issued at least 14 days before the estimate is due, excluding taxable capital gains, retirement lump sums and severance benefits — increased by 8% if the estimate is made more than 18 months after the end of that assessed year. Under-estimation penalty (Fourth Schedule para 20) is 20%: where actual taxable income is R1 million or LESS it bites only if the final estimate is below BOTH 90% of actual AND the basic amount, and is charged on the lesser of the tax on 90% of actual and the tax on the basic amount, less employees' tax and provisional tax already paid; ABOVE R1 million the basic amount gives no protection at all and the estimate must reach 80% of actual. Source: SARS Guide for Provisional Tax GEN-PT-01-G01.
_partial_years: A year may carry only the sections a calculator needs. 2025/26 has `individual`, `payroll` and `vat` — every figure in it was checked against sars.gov.za and the Budget guide — and deliberately omits SBC, turnover tax, transfer duty, CGT, estate duty and the rest, because nothing on the site uses those for a past year and publishing unverified figures is worse than publishing none. Fill a section in only when you have read it off a primary source. build.py validates whatever is present and skips what is absent.

sources.label: SARS — Rates of tax for individuals

individual._comment: SARS recorded 'no changes' to the brackets for this year, so they are identical to the year before AND to 2026/27. What moved in Budget 2026 was the rebates, the medical credits and the retirement cap — which is exactly why a year selector is worth having: the brackets look the same and the answer is not.
individual._thresholds_comment: SARS publishes these rounded to the rand; the exact quotient is 148 216.67 and 165 688.89. build.py allows a rand of slack for that.
individual._retirement_comment: R350 000 was the cap from 2016 until Budget 2026 raised it to R430 000 with effect from 1 March 2026.

provisional._comment: Dates are for a 28/29 February year of assessment, which covers every individual and most small companies. A company with another financial year-end shifts all three. Source: SARS Guide for Provisional Tax (GEN-PT-01-G01), which works this exact year as its example.

2026/27.company_period: years of assessment ending on any date from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027

individual._comment: `base` is cumulative: the tax due at the top of the bracket below. It is load-bearing — an error in one silently shifts every result above it instead of producing an obviously wrong answer. build.py --check proves each one.
individual._thresholds_comment: Derived, not independent: the threshold is the rebate divided by the first bracket rate. Stored explicitly because the guide publishes them, and checked against the rebates at build time.
individual._medical_comment: Medical scheme fees tax credit, per month.
individual._retirement_comment: Deductible up to 27.5% of the greater of remuneration or taxable income, capped annually. The cap was raised from R350 000 — a figure many calculators still use.

company._sbc_comment: Small Business Corporation rates. The R20m gross income ceiling is only ONE of six section 12E tests — the others (all shareholders natural persons, no shareholder holding an interest in another company, not more than 20% investment or personal-service income, entity type, and not being a personal service provider) cannot be judged from turnover and profit alone, so no calculator should claim to determine SBC status from figures. Limit confirmed against SARS Interpretation Note 9.
company._turnover_comment: Turnover tax for micro businesses. The widely-syndicated version of this table has an error in the third bracket — these come from the Budget guide directly. Unlike the SBC tests, the qualifying limit here IS a single checkable number, so a calculator can legitimately rule it in or out: R2.3 million of qualifying turnover, confirmed on sars.gov.za for a year of assessment ending between 1 March 2026 and 28 February 2027.

vat._threshold_comment: The compulsory threshold rose from R1 million on 1 April 2026. A great deal of South African tax content online still quotes the old figure.

exclusions._small_business_comment: Age 55+, business market value up to R15m.

transfer_duty._comment: Payable on property transactions not subject to VAT.

payroll._uif_ceiling_comment: NOT in the Budget guide, which says only 'below a certain amount'. From SARS: R17 712 per month, unchanged since 1 June 2021. Capped MONTHLY, so annualising it is only correct for steady pay.

provisional._comment: Dates are for a 28/29 February year of assessment. Source: SARS Guide for Provisional Tax (GEN-PT-01-G01).

travel._reimbursive_comment: Applies where no other travel allowance is received.

sars_interest._effective_comment: The three above apply from 1 March 2026.
sars_interest._loan_comment: Interest-free or low-interest loan fringe benefit, from 1 December 2025.
